title: Beyond the 956: Steven Hack, original 'Cats' cast member and 'Seinfeld' actor, dies at 68
excerpt: Steven Hack, the Broadway performer who spent five years in the original Broadway company of 'Cats' and went on to dozens of film and television roles including 'Seinfeld' and 'Scrubs', died November 19, 2026, at his Los Angeles home. He was 68.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Steven Hack, the Broadway performer who spent five years in the original Broadway company of Cats and went on to dozens of film and television roles, has died at 68.

Hack died on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at his home in Los Angeles after a sudden and unexpected cardiac event, according to the Interact Theatre Company, the Los Angeles nonprofit he co-founded, which announced his death on November 21. His official cause of death was atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, according to his death certificate, as reported by PEOPLE and Page Six.

Hack began his career on Broadway as a dancer, spending five years in the original Broadway company of Cats and playing Greg in the national tour of A Chorus Line. His stage credits also included Grease, The Odd Couple opposite Nathan Lane, South Pacific with Reba McEntire, and Paint Your Wagon at the Geffen Playhouse.

After moving to Los Angeles, Hack built a long screen career. His film credits included Minority Report, Intolerable Cruelty, S.W.A.T. and Thor: The Dark World. On television, he appeared in Seinfeld, Scrubs, Desperate Housewives, The West Wing, Everybody Loves Raymond, Mad About You, American Horror Story, Marvel's Agent Carter, General Hospital and Days of Our Lives. He was a member of the Television Academy for more than 20 years.

He is best remembered by many television fans for his Seinfeld appearance in the Season 7 episode "The Wig Master," in which he played a participant in an AIDS walkathon who confronts Kramer for refusing to wear a ribbon. On Scrubs, he played Dr. Bobb, a role he had recently said he hoped to revisit in the show's reboot.

Hack is survived by his sister, Karen Melnick.

Sources: PEOPLE; USA Today; Page Six; BroadwayWorld.
